chunks: When I saw that I had reached an age [of old age] and saw that I was increasing in weakness, I hastened to convey my will/advice to you, and presented salient points of it before my death overtook me suddenly, without my having disclosed to you what is in my heart, or without my judgment being impaired as my body has been impaired, or without some of the prevalences of passion and the trials of the world overtaking you before me, making you like a stubborn, shy camel.

Indeed, the heart of a youth is like empty land; it accepts whatever is strewn on it. So I hastened to educate you before your heart hardens and your intellect becomes occupied, so that you may face matters with the seriousness of your judgment, [accepting] what the people of experience have spared you the need for and the trial of. Thus, you will be saved from the burden of seeking [experience yourself], and cured from the treatment of trial, so that what we experienced comes to you, and becomes clear to you what might have been obscure to us.
ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor for the young heart in Imam Ali's advice to Hasan?
ai.summary: Delivered during the critical post-Siffin period, this instruction underscores the strategic urgency of transmitting Ali’s accumulated wisdom to Hasan before the latter’s character is hardened by the 'gale of passion' and worldly trials. It reflects the Shia emphasis on the Imam as the living repository of divine knowledge, where early pedagogical intervention ensures the heir avoids the 'cost of seeking' and the 'pain of experience' that even the Prophet’s companions endured.
